issues.problem: ko-kore example: どれが田中さんのかばんですか translated 'Which one is your bag, Mr Tanaka?'; the Japanese reads most naturally as third person, so the English adds an ambiguity.
issues.action: English changed to 'Which one is Mr Tanaka's bag?'.

issues.problem: ko-konna explain: said こんなに / そんなに go before an adjective only; they also modify verbs for degree (そんなに食べないで), so the rule as stated is incomplete.
issues.action: Rewrote: degree form こんなに etc. before an adjective or verb, with a verb example.

issues.problem: ko-context explain: 'in writing the default for referring back is そ-' omits この, which is standard in writing for the topic under discussion.
issues.action: Added (or この for the topic under discussion: この問題は...).

issues.problem: ko-context contrast: the same line 京都で古い旅館に泊まったよ was used for the あの case 'if you stayed there together', which is incoherent (you would not report it to your companion).
issues.action: Rewrote: telling someone about an inn they never saw gives その旅館; reminding a companion gives あの旅館、よかったね.

issues.problem: ko-context mistake: 子供のころ…。そのころは楽しかったなあ is not wrong; そのころ naturally refers back to the just-mentioned 子供のころ.
issues.action: Replaced with この前一緒に見たその映画 (bad) / あの映画 (good): a shared memory with nothing just mentioned, where その is plainly wrong.
